_about: Utah turf-replacement rebates by city, from the Utah Water Savers eligibility list (all pages) and each program's details page, checked 2026-10-27. A city not on the list is not eligible (no qualifying water-efficient landscape ordinance). Rates in USD per sq ft of lawn replaced. city_notes flags cities whose tier was inferred.

statewide_rules.program: Utah Water Savers Landscape Incentive Program (Utah Division of Water Resources + local water districts)
disqualifiers: Removing or killing lawn before the site visit and approval
Lawn not living and maintained at the site visit
Account not in good standing with water provider
City without a qualifying water-efficient landscape ordinance (not on the eligibility list)
Artificial turf, concrete, or non-drip irrigation in the converted area
statewide_rules.legal: Utah Code 73-10-34 (2022 H.B. 121 turf removal incentive); Utah Admin Code R653-11

city_notes.Central: Links to Weber Basin (mywaterutah.org) but not named on either WBWCD tier list; assigned the $1.25 floor that WBWCD says all district cities get. May qualify for $2.50.
city_notes.Davis County: Links to Weber Basin but unincorporated Davis County is not named on either WBWCD tier list; assigned the $1.25 floor. May qualify for $2.50 (all other Davis cities except South Weber are $2.50).
city_notes.Francis: Utah Water Savers links Francis to CUWCD rural; WBWCD's own site also lists Francis at $1.25.
city_notes.Hill Air Force Base: Links to Weber Basin but not named on either WBWCD tier list; assigned the $1.25 floor. Federal property; eligibility unclear.
city_notes.Kanesville: Unincorporated western Weber County; WBWCD lists 'Unincorporated Weber County (Except Ogden Valley)' at $2.50 - tier inferred.
city_notes.Summit: Links to Weber Basin but not named on either WBWCD tier list (ambiguous: possibly unincorporated Summit County / Summit Park, which WBWCD lists at $1.25); assigned $1.25 floor.
city_notes.Taylor: Unincorporated western Weber County; WBWCD lists 'Unincorporated Weber County (Except Ogden Valley)' at $2.50 - tier inferred.
city_notes.West Warren: Unincorporated western Weber County; WBWCD lists 'Unincorporated Weber County (Except Ogden Valley)' at $2.50 - tier inferred.

providers.name: Central Utah Water Conservancy District
providers.notes: Standard program. Lawn must be alive at the site visit; finish within 12 months; remaining lawn strips at least 8 ft wide.

providers.name: Central Utah Water Conservancy District (rural track)
providers.notes: Rural-track rate, which also covers Provo and Orem. Same rules as the standard program.

providers.name: Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District
providers.notes: Slow the Flow program. No cap stated. Park strips must meet planting-bed rules.
providers.source: https://slowtheflow.org/rebates/jordan-valley/ ('Lawn Replacement Incentive Amount = $3.00 per sq ft')

providers.name: Utah Division of Water Resources
providers.notes: Statewide program for eligible cities with no local program. Virtual pre-conversion visit; 365 days to finish; private wells not eligible.
providers.source: https://www.utahwatersavers.com/division-of-water-resources-landscape-incentive-program-details ('Incentives are for $2.00 per square foot of grass removed and replaced with water-efficient landscaping (maximum incentive amount of $50,000/application).')

providers.name: Washington County Water Conservancy District
providers.notes: Plus a temporary $1/sq ft bonus on the first 1,000 sq ft for projects finished June 9, 2026 to June 1, 2027 (Santa Clara also adds $1 on the first 500 sq ft).
providers.source: https://www.wcwcd.gov/conservation/rebates/water-efficient-landscape-rebate/ ('$2 per square foot will be paid for qualifying converted areas.')

supplemental.condition: Projects completed between June 9, 2026 and June 1, 2027

providers.name: Weber Basin Water Conservancy District
providers.notes: Landscape Lawn Exchange, higher tier for cities with a qualifying ordinance.
providers.source: https://mywaterutah.org/landscape-lawn-exchange ('After an inspection to ensure compliance with program requirements, participants living in a community that has adopted water-efficient landscape ordinances will receive $2.50 per square foot of lawn that is removed and replaced by water-efficient landscaping.')

providers.name: Weber Basin Water Conservancy District (base tier)
providers.notes: Landscape Lawn Exchange base tier; some cities may qualify for the higher tier.
providers.source: https://mywaterutah.org/landscape-lawn-exchange ('All other participants will receive an incentive of $1.25 per square foot of lawn that is remove and replaced by water-efficient landscaping.')
